text.p: These are the leading stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian head of state and chairman of Economic Community of West African States, General Sani Abacha, directs that regional troops in Liberia should provide security for its newly elected president, former warlord Charles Taylor.
- One person was confirmed to have been killed when Moslem religious fanatics clashed with police in the northern city of Kaduna earlier this week.
- Lagos received additional 39.8 million litres of fuel on Thursday to check buildup of vehicles at pump stations.
- There are no plans to reconstitute soon the board of directors of the Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Company which was recently dissolved by the oil minister, sources told Daily Times.
- Family of ailing maverick Nigerian musician Fela Anikulapo-Kuti dispel anxiety about his health, saying he is alive contrary to media reports that he is dead.
- The capital market's regulatory body, the Securities and Exchange Commission, defends plans to set up a second stock exchange in the country, saying it is healthy for competition.
- Chief of defence staff Major-General Abdulsalam Abubakar is to lead many other top brass on an official visit to China and North Korea from Friday.

- Nigeria says soldiers loyal to Sierra Leone's coup leader have attacked bases of West African troops stationed in the country despite a ceasefire agreement signed by the two sides in Abidjan last week.
- Nigeria's naira currency appreciates at weekly auction to 83.20 to the dollar from 83.50 last week as demand for forex also rises to $31.106 million from $24.614 million last week.
